title: Anti-HSV-1 antibodies: complement contribution and antibody dependence
objective: Test whether C1q-dependent complement engagement contributes to protection in neonatal mice and whether its contribution differs across antibody identities within and between gD and gB. Evidence cutoff: before 2026-01-01; preprints are explicitly labelled.
coordinate_note: All chain coordinates refer to full translated precursors including a 20-aa secretion leader. Fc edits use EU nomenclature; human heavy constant residue 1 = EU118. Each IgG is expressed from separate H and L polypeptides and assembles as 2H+2L after leader removal. The synthetic leader and common constant regions are an assumed standardized expression implementation, not an exact reconstruction of a clinical product.

sources.title: Effector functions are required for broad and potent protection of neonatal mice with antibodies targeting HSV glycoprotein D
sources.coverage: Results, main figure captions and antibody/complement assay methods inspected in full-text XML; supplements not inspected. Title confirmed on article page. CH42 AAA data do not establish the behavior of WT-Fc CH42.

sources.title: Antibodies targeting HSV glycoprotein B require effector functions to protect neonatal mice
sources.coverage: July 2025 version 1 PREPRINT, not the 2026 journal article. Results, main figure captions and recombinant antibody methods inspected in XML; supplements not inspected. Title/date confirmed on its own page.

sources.title: A non-neutralizing glycoprotein B monoclonal antibody protects against herpes simplex virus disease in mice
sources.coverage: Selected Results, structural and expression methods and figure captions inspected in XML; supplement not inspected. Title confirmed on article page. Adult murine-isotype results are a different setting from neonatal human-IgG1 chimeras.

sources.title: Prefusion structure, evasion and neutralization of HSV-1 glycoprotein B
sources.coverage: D48 structural Results, Fig. 6, Extended Data Fig. 9 captions, antibody production methods inspected in XML; supplementary files not inspected. Title/date confirmed on article page.

sources.title: Effector Function Activities of a Panel of Mutants of a Broadly Neutralizing Antibody against Human Immunodeficiency Virus Type 1
sources.coverage: Abstract inspected on primary article page and title confirmed. K322A abolished C1q binding/CDC but also reduced FcγR binding and ADCC approximately twofold in b12; no claim of FcγR neutrality is made.

sources.title: A Novel Platform for the Potentiation of Therapeutic Antibodies Based on Antigen-Dependent Formation of IgG Hexamers at the Cell Surface
sources.coverage: Selected Results, Figs. 5–7 captions and antibody engineering methods inspected in XML and primary page; supplementary captions, not files, inspected. E430G increased CDC and could also increase ADCC in another antibody.

sources.title: Improving antibody-mediated protection against HSV infection by eliminating interactions with the viral Fc receptor gE/gI
sources.coverage: Preprint Results on Fc changes, antigen binding, neutralization and viral Fc receptor, and relevant methods inspected in XML; supplements not inspected. Title verified through primary-source search.

sources.title: Eliminating interactions with the viral Fc receptor improves antibody-mediated protection against neonatal HSV infection in mice
sources.coverage: Final publication abstract inspected and title/date confirmed on primary-source search. Mechanistic details taken from the separately identified 2024 preprint, rather than assumed identical.

sources.title: Biophysical Characterization and Stability of Modified IgG1 Antibodies with Different Hexamerization Propensities
sources.coverage: Abstract/search-indexed primary PubMed record inspected; full text unavailable. Title verified in primary-source search; E430G reduced conformational stability in tested backgrounds.

sources.title: Compositions and methods for preventing or ameliorating neonatal hsv infection
sources.coverage: Table 3 VH/VL sequences, SEQ ID 26/27, inspected on primary patent publication page/search. Sequence material only, no legal interpretation.

sources.title: Compositions and methods for preventing or ameliorating neonatal HSV infection
sources.coverage: Table 1, SEQ ID 7/8, inspected. Q rather than OCR O confirmed at LQMNSLRAED and GQAPR in the granted patent. Patent text is sequence provenance, not evidence for efficacy of the proposed Fc variants.

hypotheses.question: Does C1q recruitment contribute to protection by HSV8?
hypotheses.mechanism: Reduce the C1q-interaction surface with K322A while retaining the parental Fab and glycosylation sequon.
hypotheses.measurement: WT versus K322A in complement-intact and C1q-deficient settings; require matched binding, complement-free neutralization, murine FcγR activity, viral Fc-receptor binding and exposure. A WT–KA difference that disappears on C1q removal supports complement dependence.
hypotheses.note: Loss-of-function comparison is antibody-specific; no loss at a floor/ceiling does not establish independence.

hypotheses.question: Can stronger surface Fc assembly improve complement-dependent protection by HSV8?
hypotheses.mechanism: E430G promotes antigen-dependent Fc–Fc packing, which may improve multivalent recruitment of C1q.
hypotheses.measurement: E430G versus matched WT, with C1q depletion/rescue and host C1q status. An enhancement lost upon C1q removal supports a complement-mediated gain.
hypotheses.note: This tests an opportunity for enhancement, not the necessity of basal complement activity; necessity and gain need not agree.

variants.headline: C1q-interface substitution

chains.name: Heavy-chain precursor
chains.note: Leader cleavage is intended after residue 20; verify processed N terminus. No purification tag or protease site.

chains.name: Light-chain precursor

variants.note: gD target. Neutralizing anti-gD comparator; Fc contribution depends on antibody concentration. Express H and L together, yielding two copies of each in the mature IgG.

rationale.hypothesis: Test the loss of C1q-dependent activity for this Fab.
rationale.edit: Perturbs the C1q-contact region while leaving the paired antigen-binding domains unchanged.

observations.finding: K322A removed C1q/CDC activity in b12 but changed FcγR binding and ADCC modestly.
observations.context: Human IgG1 anti-HIV b12, not this anti-HSV antibody

rationale.comparison: Matched WT is the molecular control; C1q removal and add-back provide the orthogonal mechanistic control. Compare within this antibody before comparing effect sizes across antibodies.
rationale.uncertainty: K322A is C1q-reducing, not guaranteed to be complement-selective or a complete mouse-complement knockout; FcγR and viral Fc-receptor activity must be measured.
rationale.inference: Transfer a published IgG1 perturbation to an anti-HSV Fab on the same common Fc sequence.

variants.name: HSV8 · E430G
variants.headline: Fc-packing substitution

chains.name: Heavy-chain precursor
chains.note: Leader cleavage is intended after residue 20; verify processed N terminus. No purification tag or protease site.

chains.name: Light-chain precursor
chains.note: Leader cleavage is intended after residue 20; verify processed N terminus. No purification tag or protease site.

variants.note: gD target. Neutralizing anti-gD comparator; Fc contribution depends on antibody concentration. Express H and L together, yielding two copies of each in the mature IgG.

rationale.hypothesis: Test whether improved Fc packing can raise complement-dependent protection for this Fab.
rationale.edit: Alters the Fc–Fc assembly interface without changing antigen-binding sequence.

observations.finding: E430G enhanced antigen-dependent CDC; enhanced ADCC was also observed in one tested antibody.
observations.context: Human IgG1 antibodies targeting tumor-cell antigens

rationale.comparison: Compare with this antibody’s WT and K322A. Require C1q dependence of the EG advantage rather than inferring it from higher C3 deposition alone.
rationale.uncertainty: Antigen geometry may prevent productive Fc assembly. E430G can alter other functions, self-association and stability; a gain in protection is not automatically a complement effect.
rationale.inference: Transfer an Fc-packing strategy from non-HSV antigens; no pre-cutoff result is claimed for this exact sequence.

precedent_search.scope: Independent primary-source searches for HSV gD/gB neonatal protection, C1q/complement, Fc engineering, viral Fc receptor, antibody sequences and antigen conformational accessibility, restricted to work published before 2026-01-01; main-text follow-up included 2025 gB preprint and October/November 2025 structural/vFcR studies. Search results were in hand before final candidate selection. No 2026 result used as a design observation.

study_design.production: Co-express the two chains of each construct in one common mammalian expression system. Use comparable production batches and glycoform distributions; WT CH42 explicitly lacks AAA. Purify intact IgG and document monomer, chain assembly, endotoxin and Fc glycan occupancy/composition. Signal cleavage and mature N termini must be verified; leader choice is an expression assumption.
qualification: Confirm H/L identities, 2H2L assembly, monomer fraction and active binding concentration. Verify the K322A/E430G substitutions by peptide mapping.
Measure recombinant-antigen and relevant cell-surface binding, with infected-cell binding where appropriate; normalize complement readouts to antibody occupancy.
Measure C1q binding and downstream C3 deposition using mouse complement, with C1q-depleted or genetically deficient serum and C1q reconstitution. Heat inactivation alone does not isolate C1q.
Check murine FcγR binding/function, gE/gI binding and complement-free neutralization; these are exclusion tests for an unclean mechanistic comparison.
Measure serum exposure rather than assuming equal injected mass yields equal available antibody.
study_design.host_factorial: Use the established neonatal HSV-1 protection model with complement-intact and C1q-deficient littermate-compatible cohorts. Include matched non-HSV human IgG1 and untreated controls in each host condition. Genotype-specific baseline susceptibility must be accounted for. Host/serum manipulations are experiment controls, not additional engineered antibody constructs.
study_design.exposure: Use a shared exposure framework plus antibody-specific dose/exposure ranges that avoid complete protection or complete failure. Do not interpret a single high-dose neutralizing-antibody comparison as complement independence. Establish the WT CH42 baseline rather than borrowing the AAA baseline.
study_design.outcomes: Primary: protection/survival or prespecified humane endpoint. Secondary: matched-time viral burden in nervous and systemic tissues, disease severity and complement engagement. Account for early deaths in tissue comparisons; survivors-only viral loads can bias inference.
study_design.heterogeneity: Prespecify the antibody identity × Fc variant × C1q-status interaction, with litter/experiment effects. Estimate within-antibody WT–KA effects and their uncertainty, then compare those effects directly. Significance in one antibody and nonsignificance in another is not evidence that the effects differ. Uniformity requires an adequately powered equivalence margin and informative exposure ranges; a null interaction only fails to detect heterogeneity.

interpretation.WT_over_KA_only_with_C1q: Supports a contribution of C1q-dependent complement, conditional on comparable exposure and non-complement functions.
interpretation.EG_over_WT_only_with_C1q: Supports the potential to improve protection through complement-associated activity.
interpretation.EG_over_WT_without_KA_loss: Enhancement opportunity without evidence that WT protection requires complement.
interpretation.variant_effect_persists_without_C1q: Investigate FcγR, vFcR, neutralization, aggregation or exposure differences.
interpretation.no_effect_at_floor_or_ceiling: Mechanistically inconclusive; do not call complement-independent.
interpretation.different_clean_effects_across_antibodie: Supports antibody-dependent complement contributions; four examples do not establish an antigen-wide rule.

study_design.cascade_check: For a sentinel WT/KA or WT/EG pair, remove downstream C3 activity and restore it in the serum assay. Concordant dependence on C1q and downstream complement supports cascade involvement; C1q binding alone can have other effects. Do not equate C3 deposition with membrane-attack-complex lysis.
study_design.not_measured: No expression, binding, complement, neutralization, pharmacokinetic or animal experiment was performed. No usable homolog conservation profile was produced. Required constant-region fetches refused undersized clusters; clone-name retrieval found no antibody accession-backed ortholog sets. No per-residue scores or functional predictions are fabricated.

caveats: E430G may increase reversible self-association and reduce conformational stability; screen aggregates, thermal stress and antigen-independent complement activity before interpreting a biological gain.

The common synthetic leader, VH–CH1/VL–CL junctions and BMPC-23 murine-variable/human-constant pairing can affect secretion, proteolysis or folding. Verify mature chain ends and intact monomeric 2H2L assembly.
N297 glycosylation is retained, but cell line and batch-dependent glycoforms can change both complement and FcγR functions. Match or characterize glycosylation.
K322A and E430G are not assumed perfectly selective; changes in mouse FcγR interactions, viral Fc-receptor binding or clearance can mimic complement effects.
D48 can change gB conformation; BMPC-23 recognizes a postfusion epitope. Soluble-gB binding or bead C3 deposition may not reflect epitope exposure and Fc spacing on virions or infected cells.
CH42 WT may be less protective than the published AAA version; BMPC-23 has a neonatal protection floor. Loss-of-function comparisons require measurable WT protection.
